A1.justification: Both PDFs describe OSPO and have readable text, equations, tables and figures. However, v3 repeatedly references an appendix that is absent from the supplied PDF, limiting comparison of promised implementation details and supplementary experiments with v2's included appendix.

before.justification: V2 reports original benchmark evaluations, discrimination experiments, ablations, and appendix experiments on iterative training, inference-time scaling and confirmation bias.

after.justification: V3 reports original benchmark evaluations, preference-pair diagnostics, component ablations, scaling experiments and computational-cost comparisons.

M1.justification: V3 introduces attention-derived object masks and object-weighted SimPO, replacing v2's SimPO plus conditional text-preference loss. It also replaces uncertainty-based negative selection with coupled image-pair filtering and selection by the preferred image's VQA score. These change the training objective and data-selection procedure.

E1.justification: The three main benchmarks and four training-prompt categories remain. Diagnostic coverage changes: v2 evaluates image/text discrimination using AnyEdit and SugarCrepe samples, whereas v3 analyzes preference errors in 16,000 self-generated SILMM-style pairs.

E2.justification: V3 adds Show-o2 in Table 2 and FocusDiff in the efficiency comparison. T2I-R1 disappears from Tables 1–2 but remains in Figure 6; v2's UniRL comparison is no longer supplied. DSR and SUDER correspond to the same Hong et al. work, so that renaming does not constitute a new baseline.

E3.justification: Generated training prompts increase from 19,000 to 20,000. Reported backbone experiments shift from Janus-Pro-7B, UniTok-7B and Janus-1.3B to Janus-Pro-1B/7B, with alternative-backbone results only referenced in the missing appendix. V3 also changes the sample-size sweep and introduces candidate-count sweeps and a one-iteration timing protocol.

E4.justification: V3 replaces discrimination diagnostics with preference-null/false-pair analysis, adds candidate-pair-size and efficiency studies, and revises loss and filtering/densification ablations. Dataset-size sensitivity already appeared in v2 Appendix D.3. V2's iterative-training, inference-scaling and confirmation-bias results are not supplied in v3.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or statistical significance tests. V2's model-confidence measurements concern discrimination and selection, rather than uncertainty across experimental runs.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 replace OSPO-7B results, including color 0.8438 to 0.8567, texture 0.7782 to 0.7727, DPGBench overall 85.34 to 85.61, and GenEval overall 0.82 to 0.83, under changed method/training settings. V3 also supplies new 1B, diagnostic, ablation and efficiency results, while several v2 supplementary result tables are absent.

T1.justification: V3 removes the discrimination-ratio formulation and conditional-preference term, defines mask-dependent token weights w_t = beta(1 + alpha m_t), and replaces the three-term training objective with object-weighted SimPO plus SFT. The mathematical filtering conditions also change substantially. Neither version develops theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The central methodological contribution is redefined from hard image/text preference learning with a conditional-preference loss to attention-mask-guided, object-weighted optimization. The broader claims of self-improving object-level alignment without external training resources remain.

C2.justification: The motivation shifts from weak fine-grained discrimination to noisy Best-of-N preference labels. V3 explains improvements through object-focused gradients and SFT structural anchoring, and introduces a counting limitation associated with self-generated training data. V2's detailed confirmation-bias interpretation is no longer supplied.

D1.justification: V3 provides new mask/loss defaults and reports eight rather than four A100 80GB GPUs. However, v2's Table 7 training specifications—including LoRA, optimizer, learning rates, steps and batch sizes—and Appendix F prompt templates are absent. V3 directs readers to an unavailable appendix for these details and further mask algorithms.

R1.justification: Beyond moving related work from Appendix A into Section 2, v3 expands its positioning against external-feedback PPO/DPO methods and adds literature on attention-based grounding, prompt optimization, decompositional evaluation and FocusDiff. It explicitly situates prompt densification as an extension of prior approaches.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, method and analysis narrative are extensively rewritten. V3 introduces numbered sections, moves related work into the main text, embeds the preliminary study within the framework section, and reorganizes the method into five stages and analyses into dedicated subsections.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is substantially redrawn around masks and the revised pipeline. V3 replaces diagnostic displays, adds candidate-size and efficiency plots, restructures benchmark tables by model size, and combines filtering/densification comparisons. Qualitative panels are reorganized with some reused examples; v2's appendix displays are largely absent.

improvement.justification: V3 offers clearer organization and useful new pair-quality, candidate-size and efficiency analyses. These benefits coexist with a substantial loss of supplied reproducibility information and supplementary evidence: unlike v2, its repeatedly referenced appendix is missing. Changed methods and training settings also prevent interpreting revised scores as controlled gains. The available PDFs therefore do not establish a reliable net improvement or deterioration.
